answerNotes.PEACH: A peach has a fuzzy skin and a hard pit. A nectarine is a close relative with smooth skin.
answerNotes.SWEET: Sweet describes flavor, not temperature or texture. A food can be sweet and cold, or sweet and warm.
answerNotes.RIPE: Ripe means ready to eat or harvest. Ripeness and color do not have exactly the same relationship in every kind of fruit.
answerNotes.JUICE: Juice is liquid released from fruit or vegetables. Pulp is the soft plant material that may remain mixed into it.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.PRICE: Price is the amount asked for an item. Change is money returned after a customer pays more than that amount.
answerNotes.SIGN: Sign can be a public notice or the action of writing a name. Check whether the clue describes an object or asks for a verb.
answerNotes.ROAD: A road is a route for vehicles. A sidewalk or footpath provides a different part of the journey for people on foot.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.
answerNotes.FRUIT: Everyday fruit dishes can mix several kinds of plant produce. The serving word is culinary and does not require a botanical classification.

words: Handle turned to operate a mechanism
Frozen dairy dessert scooped into a cone (two words)
Sweet flavor often used in ice cream
To change water from liquid to solid
Part held when carrying or using something

answerNotes.CREAM: Cream is the rich part of milk. Whipping adds air, which is why whipped cream becomes fluffy.
answerNotes.MILK: Milk is a dairy liquid used in drinks and batters. Cream is the richer portion, with a higher fat content.
answerNotes.SUGAR: Sugar sweetens baking mixtures and drinks. Granulated sugar and powdered sugar have different textures despite sharing the same sweet ingredient.
answerNotes.ICE: Ice is solid water. It absorbs heat as it melts, which helps cool a drink.
answerNotes.SALT: Salt is a seasoning usually paired with pepper on the table. A pinch describes a small amount rather than a special kind of it.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.

answerNotes.FLAG: A flag can be a cloth symbol or a small signaling marker. A mailbox flag shows a postal signal rather than identifying a country.
answerNotes.STAR: A star can mean a distant sun or a pointed decorative shape. Christmas ornaments represent the shape rather than an actual celestial object.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.POLE: A barber pole's stripes traditionally identify the shop. The moving pattern can make the stripes appear to travel upward or downward.
answerNotes.PORCH: A porch is an outdoor entrance area, often with a roof. A patio is usually a paved sitting area at ground level.
answerNotes.JULY: July is the seventh month. The Fourth of July is the U.S. Independence Day holiday.

answerNotes.MUSTARD: Mustard names a plant as well as a condiment made from its seeds. The parable concerns the small seed and its growing plant.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.TICKET: A ticket can give admission or identify an item left for a service. A theater ticket and a dry-cleaning claim ticket serve different uses.
answerNotes.SAUCE: A sauce adds moisture or flavor to another food. It can be smooth, chunky, hot, or cold.
answerNotes.HOT: Hot describes temperature. A hot dog is a food name, so the two-word phrase has a meaning beyond the adjective alone.
answerNotes.YELLOW: Yellow is a color name rather than a material. The movie's yellow brick road combines a color with a building block.

answerNotes.TOMATO: Tomatoes are used like vegetables in savory cooking. Botanically, their seed-bearing fruits belong in the fruit category.
answerNotes.SANDWICH: A sandwich places a filling between pieces of bread. An open-faced version uses just one supporting slice.
answerNotes.BREAD: Bread may be a whole loaf or pieces cut from it. A loaf is counted as a whole, while a slice is one flat portion.
answerNotes.RIPE: Ripe means ready to eat or harvest. Ripeness and color do not have exactly the same relationship in every kind of fruit.
answerNotes.JUICE: Juice is liquid released from fruit or vegetables. Pulp is the soft plant material that may remain mixed into it.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.SALT: Salt is a seasoning usually paired with pepper on the table. A pinch describes a small amount rather than a special kind of it.
answerNotes.GARDEN: A garden is an area cultivated for plants. A single bed or plot can be one part of a larger garden.
answerNotes.SUMMER: Summer scenes use familiar warm-weather outings. Actual temperatures and traditions differ between regions and families.
answerNotes.PLATE: A plate is flatter than a bowl. Its broad surface is useful for separate portions of a meal.
